title: Orchestrate multi-region failover with warm-standby readiness probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Redwood's smart routing currently supports region selection and tier routing, but does not have an orchestrated multi-region failover flow with proactive warm-standby readiness checks. Without coordinated orchestration, failovers can cause capacity shocks, cold-start latencies, and noisy errors for customers using Dedicated and Private deployments.

Goal: Implement an orchestration layer and runtime primitives that: (1) perform periodic readiness probes against warm-standby capacity in secondary regions, (2) maintain a per-customer readiness state used by the routing policy engine, and (3) execute controlled failover transitions that respect tier routing, model variant compatibility, and traffic shaping (canary/gradual shift).

Scope: This ticket covers design and an engineering PoC to: define readiness probe semantics, extend routing policy schema, add a readiness cache with TTL and staleness bounds, implement failover orchestration state machine, and add observability/alerts. It excludes long-term autoscaling improvements (tracked in ENG-49821) and UI work in the Console (tracked in PM-321).

Non-goals: Rewriting autoscaler heuristics, customer self-serve UI for editing probes (Console work will follow), and on-prem HSM/KMS changes.

High-level approach:
- Define a small, deterministic readiness probe protocol (health endpoint + synthetic request path) run from the control plane into warm-standby pools.
- Store probe results in a per-customer readiness map with time-based decay and provenance (probe time, latency, model-variant).
- Extend routing policy object to include policy.failover.order (region priority), policy.failover.warm_standby.probe_profile (interval, timeout, success_threshold), and policy.failover.transition.strategy (immediate | canary-percent | gradual-over-seconds).
- Implement an orchestrator that evaluates readiness state, verifies model-variant compatibility (fallback_model_map), and initiates traffic shift using per-route traffic weight updates to the serving control plane.
- Add hooks for safety checks: capacity headroom, SLA tier checks, and a rollback window with automatic revert on error spikes.

Success metrics:
- Mean additional latency introduced by readiness probes < 50ms per probe on average.
- Time to shift 100% traffic to healthy region under canary-disabled policy: < 30s when warm-standby is healthy.
- Reduction in failover-induced 5xxs across canary customers by 80% vs baseline (measured across synthetic chaos test).
- Probability of false-positive readiness (standby marked healthy but fails under load) < 1% in synthetic trials.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Probes produce false confidence because warm-standby not warmed for specific KV state. Mitigation: Probe includes synthetic prefix and cached KV-key checks when supported; we also require minimum warm-up QPS before full shift.
- Risk: Routing config desync between control plane and edge. Mitigation: Implement versioned rollout tokens and verify edge ACKs before traffic cutover.
- Risk: Cost of continuous probes. Mitigation: Adaptive probe intervals based on customer tier and recent churn; default to lower frequency for P3 customers.

Open questions:
- Should probe payloads exercise quantized kernels vs full float kernels for compatibility? (Research required; see links)
- What hard limits should we enforce for auto-retries of failed readiness checks?

Deliverables:
- RFC design doc describing probe protocol, policy schema, and orchestrator state machine.
- Prototype implementation under runtime/orchestrator with feature flag.
- Integration tests and synthetic chaos test that simulates regional outage and measures behavior.
- Monitoring dashboards and SLOs for readiness probes and failover incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Probe protocol RFC merged and reviewed by runtime + SRE
Routing policy schema extended and validated by API tests
Orchestrator prototype performs controlled canary shifts to a healthy warm-standby region under feature flag
Automated test that simulates primary-region outage and asserts <30s full-shift when warm-standby healthy
Dashboards for probe success-rate, probe latency, and failover events created and linked
rollout_plan: 1) Merge RFC and schema changes behind feature flag. 2) Deploy probe runner to control plane with conservative defaults (interval=60s, timeout=2s) for internal test customers. 3) Run synthetic chaos tests against canary tenants. 4) Enable canary traffic shifts for a subset of low-risk customers. 5) Gradually widen based on metrics and runbook checks. 6) Hand over Console toggle to PM for customer opt-in.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe logic and TTL cache, integration tests for routing policy parsing, end-to-end synthetic scenario: simulate primary region killed and assert orchestrator shifts to standby per configured strategy, run load trial to validate warm-standby under QPS. Include negative tests for model-variant incompatibility and ensure rollback path triggers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create metrics: readiness_probe_success_rate, readiness_probe_latency_ms_p50/p95, failover_initiated_count, failover_success_rate, failover_rollbacks. Alerts: probe_success_rate < 90% for 5m for P0 customers, failover_rollbacks > 1 within 10m triggers P1 investigation. Link dashboards in RFC.
